The '''2018–19 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|115th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|88th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. It covered a period from 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2019. The season is widely described as one of the worst campaigns in the club's modern history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/real-madrid-need-four-goals-to-avoid-their-worst-season-ever-in-21st-century-633914|title=Real Madrid need four goals to avoid their worst season ever in 21st century|date=May 14, 2019|website=BeSoccer|access-date=May 19, 2019|archive-date=January 10, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110032057/https://www.besoccer.com/new/real-madrid-need-four-goals-to-avoid-their-worst-season-ever-in-21st-century-633914|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was also the first season since [[2008–09 Real Madrid CF season|2008–09]] without the club's record goalscorer [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], who departed for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the summer of 2018, having won 15 trophies altogether since his debut.

==Summary==
===Pre-season===
After [[Zinedine Zidane]]'s departure,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44315700|title=Zinedine Zidane: Real Madrid boss stands down five days after Champions League win|work=BBC Sport|date=31 May 2018|access-date=31 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/05/zidane-real-madrid-gave-me-everything-and-i-will-remain-close-to-the-club-forever|title=Zidane: "Real Madrid gave me everything and I will remain close to the club forever"|date=31 May 2018|work=realmadrid.com}}</ref> Madrid announced on 12 June 2018, that [[Julen Lopetegui]] would take over the head coaching position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/06/official-announcement-julen-lopetegui-will-be-the-real-madrid-coach-after-the-celebration-of-the-2018-world-cup|title=Official Announcement: Julen Lopetegui will be the Real Madrid coach after the celebration of the 2018 World Cup|publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]|date=12 June 2018}}</ref>

On 22 June 2018, Madrid announced their first signing of the season, adding [[Andriy Lunin]] to the squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/06/official-announcement-andriy-lunin|title=Official Announcement: Andriy Lunin|publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]|date=22 June 2018}}</ref> On 5 July 2018, Madrid signed [[Álvaro Odriozola]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/07/official-announcement-alvaro-odriozola|title=Official Announcement: Álvaro Odriozola|publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]|date=5 July 2018}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid agreed to sell [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] for €117 million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Cristiano Ronaldo|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/07/official-announcement-cristiano-ronaldo|access-date=10 July 2018|agency=realmadrid.com|date=10 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44785173|title=Cristiano Ronaldo: Juventus sign Real Madrid forward for £99.2m|date=10 July 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=10 July 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref>

[[Thibaut Courtois]] joined Madrid on 8 August 2018 from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Official announcement: Thibaut Courtois|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/official-announcement-thibaut-courtois|access-date=8 August 2018|agency=realmadrid.com|date=8 August 2018}}</ref> while [[Mateo Kovačić]] moved to Chelsea on loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2018/8/8/courtois-and-kovacic-deals-agreed|title=Courtois and Kovacic deals agreed|date=8 August 2018|work=chelseafc.com}}</ref>

===August===
The season started on 15 August, with the [[2018 UEFA Super Cup]] against [[Atlético Madrid]]. The game was lost 2–4 after extra time. [[Karim Benzema]] and [[Sergio Ramos]] gave Madrid the 2–1 lead which was cancelled out late in the second half. It was Real's first European finals loss after nine consecutive wins.<ref>{{cite news|title=2–4: The Super Cup is decided in extra time|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/2-4-the-super-cup-is-decided-in-extra-time|access-date=15 August 2018|agency=realmadrid.com|date=15 August 2018}}</ref> The new [[2018–19 La Liga|La Liga season]] started with a 2–0 victory against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] four days later, with goals from [[Dani Carvajal]] and [[Gareth Bale]].<ref>{{cite news|title=2–0: Real Madrid kick off LaLiga campaign with deserved win|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/2-0-real-madrid-kick-off-laliga-campaign-with-deserved-win|access-date=19 August 2018|agency=realmadrid.com|date=19 August 2018}}</ref> Against [[Girona FC|Girona]], Madrid came out with a 4–1 victory from behind, with a brace from Benzema and goals from Ramos and Bale.<ref>{{cite news|title=1–4: Real Madrid fight back against Girona to go top|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/1-4-real-madrid-fight-back-against-girona-to-go-top|access-date=26 August 2018|agency=realmadrid.com|date=26 August 2018}}</ref> On 29 August 2018, [[Mariano Díaz]] returned to Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Mariano|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/official-announcement-mariano|access-date=29 August 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=29 August 2018}}</ref>

===September===
On the first day of the new month, a brace from Benzema and goals from Bale and Ramos secured Madrid three points in a 4–1 win over [[CD Leganés|Leganés]].<ref>{{cite news|title=4–1: Real Madrid run riot to stay top|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/4-1-real-madrid-run-riot-to-stay-top|access-date=1 September 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=1 September 2018}}</ref> The away game at [[Athletic Bilbao]], on 15 September 2018, ended in a 1–1 draw with the lone goal coming from [[Isco]].<ref>{{cite news|title=1–1: Real Madrid unfortunate not to get more at San Mamés|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/1-1-real-madrid-unfortunate-not-to-get-more-at-san-mames|access-date=15 September 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=15 September 2018}}</ref> Four days later, in the first match of the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League]] [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]], Madrid defeated [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] 3–0 after goals from Bale, Isco and Mariano.<ref>{{cite news|title=3–0: The European champions start in formidable fashion|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/3-0-the-european-champions-start-in-formidable-fashion|access-date=19 September 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=19 September 2018}}</ref> [[Marco Asensio]] scored the lone goal in a 1–0 win over [[RCD Espanyol]], just three days later.<ref>{{cite news|title=1–0: Asensio's goal clinches the win over Espanyol|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/1-0-asensios-goal-clinches-the-win-over-espanyol|access-date=22 September 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=22 September 2018}}</ref> The first defeat of the league season came on 26 September 2018, against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], with Real losing 0–3.<ref>{{cite news|title=3–0: Real Madrid slump to defeat at the Sánchez-Pizjuán|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/3-0-real-madrid-slump-to-defeat-at-the-sanchez-pizjuan|access-date=26 September 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=26 September 2018}}</ref> In the first league [[Madrid derby]] against Atlético, the match ended in a goalless draw three days later.<ref>{{cite news|title=0–0: Madrid kept probing for a breakthrough until the last|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/0-0-madrid-kept-probing-for-a-breakthrough-until-the-last|access-date=29 September 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=29 September 2018}}</ref>

===October===
[[File:Marco Asensio 2018.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[Marco Asensio]] in an away [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League group stage|Champions League group stage]] [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group G|game]] against [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], with the left sleeve of his shirt prominently featuring an updated UCL [[European Champion Clubs' Cup#Multiple-winner badge|multiple-winner badge]], courtesy of Madrid's triumph in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2018 edition]]]]
On 2 October 2018, the Champions League match at [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] ended in a 0–1 loss.<ref>{{cite news|title=1–0: Woodwork denies Madrid in Moscow|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/1-0-woodwork-denies-madrid-in-moscow|access-date=2 October 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=2 October 2018}}</ref> Four days later, against [[Deportivo Alavés]], Madrid lost 0–1 again.<ref>{{cite news|title=1–0: Added time goal spells defeat in Vitoria|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/1-0-added-time-goal-spells-defeat-in-vitoria|access-date=6 October 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=6 October 2018}}</ref> Their next game was a 1–2 loss against [[Levante UD]] on 20 October 2018, with the lone goal coming from [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]].<ref>{{cite news|title=1–2: Levante result is harsh on Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/1-2-levante-result-is-harsh-on-madrid|access-date=20 October 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=20 October 2018}}</ref> The Champions League match against [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Viktoria Plzeň]] three days later ended with a 2–1 win with goals from Benzema and Marcelo.<ref>{{cite news|title=2–1: Benzema and Marcelo goals see Madrid to victory|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/2-1-benzema-and-marcelo-goals-see-madrid-to-victory|access-date=23 October 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=23 October 2018}}</ref> Five days later, [[El Clásico]] was lost 1–5, with the goal coming from Marcelo. It was Madrid's biggest away defeat to Barcelona since 0–5 in [[2010–11 Real Madrid CF season#Matches|2010]].<ref>{{cite news|title=5–1: Real Madrid lose el Clásico|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/5-1-real-madrid-lose-el-clasico|access-date=28 October 2018|publisher=Real Madrid|date=28 October 2018}}</ref> On 29 October 2018, Lopetegui was sacked and replaced by interim coach [[Santiago Solari]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/official-announcement-5|title=Official Announcement|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=29 October 2018|access-date=29 October 2018}}</ref> On the last day of the month, Madrid took on [[UD Melilla]] in the [[2018–19 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] round of 32 first leg and won 4–0 after goals from Benzema, Asensio, Odriozola and [[Cristo González]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/0-4-madrid-put-one-foot-in-the-copa-del-rey-last-sixteen|title=0–4: Madrid put one foot in the Copa del Rey last-sixteen|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=31 October 2018|access-date=31 October 2018}}</ref>

===November===
On 3 November 2018, late goals from [[Vinícius Júnior]] and Ramos gave Madrid a 2–0 victory over [[Real Valladolid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/2-0-a-hard-earned-win-at-the-bernabeu|title=2–0: A hard earned win at the Bernabéu|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=3 November 2018|access-date=3 November 2018}}</ref> Four days later, the return game at Viktoria Plzeň in the Champions League ended with a 5–0 win, Benzema scored a brace and Bale, [[Casemiro]] and [[Toni Kroos]] each added one goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/0-5-whites-dish-out-masterclass-to-move-top-of-group|title=0–5: Whites dish out masterclass to move top of group|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=7 November 2018|access-date=7 November 2018}}</ref> Madrid defeated [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] 4–2 on 11 November 2018, after goals from Benzema, Ramos, [[Dani Ceballos]] and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/2-4-benzema-leads-the-whites-to-a-fourth-consecutive-win|title=2–4: Benzema leads the Whites to a fourth consecutive win|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=11 November 2018|access-date=11 November 2018}}</ref> Solari was upgraded to a full-time head coach on 13 November 2018, after signing a contract through 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/official-announcement-solari|title=Official Announcement: Solari|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=13 November 2018|access-date=13 November 2018}}</ref> The away game at [[SD Eibar]] on 24 November 2018 was lost 0–3.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/3-0-madrid-succumb-to-defeat-in-eibar|title=3–0: Madrid succumb to defeat in Éibar|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=24 November 2018|access-date=25 November 2018}}</ref> Three days later, the Champions League match at Roma was won 2–0 by goals from Bale and [[Lucas Vázquez]]. With that win, Madrid advanced to the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout stage]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/0-2-victory-in-rome-secures-round-of-16-spot-as-group-winners|title=0–2: Victory in Rome secures round-of-16 spot as group winners|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=27 November 2018|access-date=27 November 2018}}</ref>

===December===
On the first day of the month, an own goal and a goal from Vázquez secured Madrid three points with a 2–0 win over [[Valencia CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/2-0-key-win-over-valencia|title=2–0: Key win over Valencia|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=1 December 2018|access-date=1 December 2018}}</ref> The return leg of the Copa del Rey round of 32 tie against Melilla on 6 December 2018 was won 6–1, giving Madrid a 10–1 victory on aggregate. Asensio and Isco scored a brace each, with the remaining goals coming from Vinícius and [[Javi Sánchez (footballer)|Javi Sánchez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/6-1-into-the-last-sixteen-of-the-copa-in-style|title=6–1: Into the last-sixteen of the Copa in style|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=6 December 2018|access-date=6 December 2018}}</ref> Three days later, a Bale goal gave Real a 1–0 victory over [[SD Huesca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/0-1-bale-volley-gives-the-whites-the-win-in-huesca|title=0–1: Bale Volley gives the Whites the win in Huesca|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=9 December 2018|access-date=9 December 2018}}</ref> On 12 December 2018, Madrid suffered a 0–3 loss against CSKA Moscow on the last matchday of the Champions League group stage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/0-3-real-madrid-finish-top-of-the-group-despite-losing-to-cska|title=0–3: Real Madrid finish top of the group despite losing to CSKA|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=12 December 2018|access-date=12 December 2018}}</ref> A lone goal by Benzema helped Madrid to win 1–0 against [[Rayo Vallecano]] on 15 December 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/1-0-a-benzema-goal-enough-to-see-real-madrid-past-rayo|title=1–0: A Benzema goal enough to see Real Madrid past Rayo|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=15 December 2018|access-date=15 December 2018}}</ref> On 19 December 2018, the semi-final of the [[2018 FIFA Club World Cup]] was won 3–1 against [[Kashima Antlers]] with a hat-trick from Bale.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/1-3-bale-hat-trick-sends-real-madrid-to-the-club-world-cup-final|title=1–3: Bale Hat-trick sends Real Madrid to the Club World Cup final|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=19 December 2018|access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid defeated [[Al Ain FC|Al-Ain]] 4–1 in the [[2018 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] after goals from [[Luka Modrić]], [[Marcos Llorente]], Ramos and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/4-1-a-seventh-club-world-cup-title|title=4–1: A seventh Club World Cup title|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=22 December 2018|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref>

===January===
In the first game of the new year on 3 January 2019, Madrid drew [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 2–2 with goals from Benzema and [[Raphaël Varane]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/2-2-madrid-start-the-year-with-a-draw-at-villarreal|title=2–2: Madrid start the year with a draw at Villarreal|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=3 January 2019|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref> Three days later, the match against [[Real Sociedad]] was lost 0–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/0-2-controversial-defeat-against-real-sociedad|title=0–2: Controversial defeat against Real Sociedad|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=6 January 2019|access-date=6 January 2019}}</ref> On 6 January 2019, Madrid announced the signing of [[Brahim Díaz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/official-announcement-brahim-diaz|title=Official Announcement: Brahim Díaz|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=6 January 2019|access-date=14 January 2019}}</ref> Goals from Ramos, Vázquez and Vinícius gave Madrid a 3–0 first leg win against Leganés on 9 January 2019 in the Copa del Rey round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/3-0-real-madrid-pick-up-a-convincing-win-to-move-closer-to-copa-del-rey-quarter-finals|title=3–0: Real Madrid pick up a convincing win to move closer to Copa del Rey quarter-finals|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=9 January 2019|access-date=9 January 2019}}</ref> On 13 January 2019, a late goal from Ceballos gave Madrid a 2–1 away win against [[Real Betis]] after Modrić scored the other goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/1-2-a-ceballos-goal-gives-madrid-the-win-over-betis|title=1–2: A Ceballos goal gives Madrid the win over Betis|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=13 January 2019|access-date=13 January 2019}}</ref> Despite a 0–1 loss in the second leg three days later, an aggregate 3–1 victory over Leganés secured Madrid a place in the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/1-0-real-madrid-are-in-the-quarter-finals-of-the-copa|title=1-0: Real Madrid are in the quarter-finals of the Copa|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=16 January 2019|access-date=16 January 2019}}</ref> [[Kiko Casilla]] joined [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 17 January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leedsunited.com/news/team-news/24407/leeds-united-sign-kiko-casilla|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119174418/https://www.leedsunited.com/news/team-news/24407/leeds-united-sign-kiko-casilla|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2019|title=Leeds United sign Kiko Casilla|publisher=Leeds United F.C|date=17 January 2019|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref> Two days later, Madrid defeated Sevilla 2–0 with goals from Casemiro and Modrić.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/2-0-casemiro-and-modric-seal-a-fine-win-for-madrid|title=2–0: Casemiro and Modric seal a fine win for Madrid|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=19 January 2019|access-date=19 January 2019}}</ref> A brace from Ramos and goals by Vázquez and Benzema helped Madrid to get a 4–2 first leg home victory over Girona in the Copa del Rey quarter-finals of on 24 January.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/4-2-real-madrid-move-a-step-closer-to-the-semi-finals|title=4-2: Real Madrid move a step closer to the semi-finals|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=24 January 2019|access-date=24 January 2019}}</ref> Three days later, Real recorded another 4–2 victory, this time over Espanyol, with two goals from Benzema and goals from Ramos and Bale.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/2-4-benzema-brace-sets-up-big-win-for-the-whites|title=2–4: Benzema brace sets up big win for the Whites|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=27 January 2019|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref> On 31 January, Madrid defeated Girona 3–1 away from home to close out the month and progress to the Copa del Rey semi-finals with a 7–3 aggregate victory. Benzema scored a brace and [[Marcos Llorente|Llorente]] added another goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/01/31/copa_del_rey/1548962008_372790.html|title = Girona 1 - Real Madrid 3: Resumen, resultado y goles|date = 31 January 2019}}</ref>

===February===
On 3 February, Madrid won 3–0 against Alavés after goals from Benzema, Vinicius and Mariano.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/3-0-goals-for-madrid-as-they-record-their-fifth-consecutive-win|title=3–0: Goals for Madrid as they record their fifth consecutive win|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=3 February 2019|access-date=3 February 2019}}</ref> The first leg of the Copa del Rey semi-finals against Barcelona on 6 February ended with a 1–1 draw after Vázquez initially gave Madrid the lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/1-1-place-in-the-final-up-for-grabs-at-the-bernabeu|title=1–1: Place in the final up for grabs at the Bernabéu|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=6 February 2019|access-date=6 February 2019}}</ref> Three days later, Real won the derby against Atlético 3–1 after goals from Casemiro, Ramos and Bale to move up to the second place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/1-3-real-madrid-win-a-lively-derby-at-the-metropolitano|title=1–3: Real Madrid win a lively derby at the Metropolitano|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=9 February 2019|access-date=9 February 2019}}</ref> In the first leg of the Champions League round of 16 against [[AFC Ajax]] on 13 February, Madrid came away with a 2–1 victory, with Benzema and Asensio scoring the goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/1-2-the-champions-take-the-first-step-towards-the-quarter-finals|title=1–2: The champions take the first step towards the quarter-finals|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=13 February 2019|access-date=13 February 2019}}</ref> Four days later, Girona defeated Madrid with a score of 2–1, with the lone goal coming from Casemiro. The result meant Atlético had again overtaken Real for the second place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/1-2-the-whites-slip-up-against-girona|title=1–2: The Whites slip up against Girona|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=17 February 2019|access-date=17 February 2019}}</ref> A 2–1 victory over Levante was recorded on 24 February, after goals from Benzema and Bale, both being penalties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/1-2-madrid-win-in-valencia-ahead-of-the-clasicos|title=1–2: Madrid win in Valencia ahead of the Clásicos|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=24 February 2019|access-date=24 February 2019}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid was knocked out of the Copa del Rey by Barcelona after a 0–3 second leg defeat, resulting in a 1–4 aggregate loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/0-3-real-madrid-fail-to-make-it-to-the-copa-final|title=0–3: Real Madrid fail to make it to the Copa final|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=27 February 2019|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref>

===March===
The league Clásico took place on 2 March and was lost 0–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/03/0-1-real-madrid-tried-in-vain-to-the-last|title=0–1: Real Madrid tried in vain to the last|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=2 March 2019|access-date=2 March 2019}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid suffered a 1–4 home defeat in the return leg of the Champions League round of 16 against Ajax and was eliminated 3–5 on aggregate to end their 3–year European reign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/03/1-4-holders-bow-out-of-champions-league|title=1–4: Holders bow out of Champions League|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=5 March 2019|access-date=5 March 2019}}</ref> On 10 March, the game against Valladolid was won 4–1 after a brace from Benzema and goals from Varane and Modrić.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/03/1-4-come-back-and-a-benzema-brace|title=1–4: Come back and a Benzema brace|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=10 March 2019|access-date=10 March 2019}}</ref> Zidane returned as the head coach the next day while Solari was sacked.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/03/official-announcement|title=Official Announcement|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=11 March 2019|access-date=11 March 2019}}</ref> On 16 March, Celta Vigo was defeated 2–0 with goals from Isco and Bale.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/03/2-0-isco-and-bale-clinch-a-winning-return-for-zidane|title=2–0: Isco and Bale clinch a winning return for Zidane|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=16 March 2019|access-date=16 March 2019}}</ref> On the last day of the month, goals from Isco, Ceballos and a late one from Benzema secured Madrid three points in a 3–2 win over Huesca.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/03/3-2-moment-of-genius-from-benzema-secures-win-over-huesca|title=3–2: Moment of genius from Benzema secures win over Huesca|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=31 March 2019|access-date=31 March 2019}}</ref>

===April===
On 3 April, the away game at Valencia was lost 1–2, with the lone goal coming from Benzema in added time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/2-1-defeat-at-mestalla|title=2–1: Defeat at Mestalla|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=3 April 2019|access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref> Three days later, a brace from Benzema secured Madrid a 2–1 win over Eibar.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/2-1-benzema-double-caps-off-a-comeback-win-over-eibar|title=2–1: Benzema double caps off a comeback win over Éibar|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=6 April 2019|access-date=6 April 2019}}</ref> On 15 April, Madrid got a 1–1 draw at Leganés with a goal from Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/1-1-real-madrid-in-butarque-stalemate|title=1–1: Real Madrid in Butarque stalemate|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=15 April 2019|access-date=15 April 2019}}</ref> A hat-trick from Benzema secured Madrid a 3–0 win over Athletic Bilbao on 21 April 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/3-0-benzema-hat-trick-and-victory-over-athletic|title=3–0: Benzema hat-trick and victory over Athletic|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=21 April 2019|access-date=21 April 2019}}</ref> On 25 April, Madrid was held to a scoreless draw at Getafe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/0-0-a-goalless-draw-in-getafe|title=0–0: A goalless draw in Getafe|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=25 April 2019|access-date=25 April 2019}}</ref> Three days later, the away game at Vallecano was lost 0–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/1-0-real-madrid-lose-in-vallecas|title=1–0: Real Madrid lose in Vallecas|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=28 April 2019|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref>

===May===
On 5 May, Madrid defeated Villarreal 3–2 with a brace from Mariano and a goal from [[Jesús Vallejo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/05/3-2-win-over-villarreal-in-a-fantastic-clash-at-the-bernabeu|title=3–2: Win over Villarreal in a fantastic clash at the Bernabéu|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=5 May 2019|access-date=5 May 2019}}</ref> A week later, the away game at Real Sociedad was lost 1–3, with the lone goal coming from Brahim Díaz. With that result, Real Madrid was confirmed to finish no higher than third in the league standings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/05/3-1-defeat-in-san-sebastian|title=3–1: Defeat in San Sebastián|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=12 May 2019|access-date=12 May 2019}}</ref> The last game of the season was lost 0–2 at home to Real Betis on 19 May 2019, marking an end to a disastrous campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/05/0-2-betis-victorious-at-the-bernabeu|title=0–2: Betis victorious at the Bernabéu|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=19 May 2019|access-date=19 May 2019}}</ref> Real finished the season with the worst points total since [[2001–02 La Liga|2001–02]] and worst goal difference since [[1999–2000 La Liga|1999–2000]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2019/5/23/18632360/real-madrids-2018-2019-season-overview|title=Real Madrid's 2018–2019 Season Overview|date=23 May 2019|website=Managing Madrid}}</ref> A day later, Kroos signed a new contract until 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/05/toni-kroos-signed-his-contract-extension-with-real-madrid|title=Toni Kroos signed his contract extension with Real Madrid|publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]|date=20 May 2019|access-date=20 May 2019}}</ref>
